package_info.package_manager: stand-alone JavaScript file (Windows environment, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious JS files distributed in campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The JavaScript files are crafted to exploit a Windows zero-day vulnerability in the Mark-of-the-Web (MoTW) feature, bypassing security warnings and automatically executing ransomware payloads (Magniber) upon user interaction. The files are intentionally malformed to evade normal security controls, enabling silent malware installation.

execution_context.trigger: user double-clicks or opens the downloaded JS file (runtime)
execution_context.file_location: stand-alone .js file, downloaded from the Internet (with MoTW alternate data stream)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a WScript.Shell ActiveX object and executes a PowerShell command to run a ransomware payload, resulting in Magniber ransomware installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code uses Windows Script Host to launch a PowerShell process, which is a common technique for malware delivery. The script is designed to execute automatically without user consent due to the MoTW bypass.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal JavaScript files should not launch PowerShell or execute arbitrary binaries, especially upon being opened from the Internet. The expected behavior is to prompt a security warning, but this is bypassed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use similar scripts for automation, but not in files distributed as fake software updates or with malformed signatures.
key_indicators: Execution of PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass
No user interaction required for payload execution

execution_context.trigger: file open (runtime), after download from Internet
execution_context.file_location: malformed Authenticode-signed .js file (signature section tampered via hex editor)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malformed Authenticode signature causes Windows to skip MoTW security warnings, allowing the malicious JavaScript to execute automatically.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Tampering with the Authenticode signature to bypass security controls is a clear sign of malicious intent. This manipulation is not required for legitimate software distribution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Signed files are expected to have valid, untampered signatures. Modifying the signature to evade security checks is abnormal.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. Legitimate use would involve valid signing, not tampering.
key_indicators: Signature section altered via hex editor
MoTW flag present but security warning not shown

attack_chain.action: Threat actor crafts a malicious JavaScript file with a malformed Authenticode signature to bypass MoTW warnings.
attack_chain.leads_to: User downloads and opens the file

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious JavaScript file, expecting a security warning, but none appears due to the signature manipulation.
Malicious JavaScript executes a PowerShell command to run the Magniber ransomware payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware is installed and executed on the victim's system

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript files invoking WScript.Shell or similar objects to launch PowerShell or other processes
Execution of PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass from a .js file
Absence of MoTW security warning despite file being downloaded from the Internet
file_indicators: JavaScript files with malformed or invalid Authenticode signatures
Presence of MoTW alternate data stream (Zone.Identifier) but no security prompt
Unusual or unexpected .js files in download directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections initiated by PowerShell or processes spawned from JavaScript files
Connections to known Magniber C2 infrastructure (if available from threat intel feeds)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript files that launch PowerShell or other processes, especially those downloaded from the Internet. Check for .js files with malformed Authenticode signatures or those that bypass MoTW warnings. Alert on PowerShell executions with ExecutionPolicy Bypass originating from WScript or cscript.exe. Correlate with user download activity and absence of expected security prompts.
